trickyParts: The construct keeps the old flow construct's reading through a resolveAll on the document construct: it rewrites the lineEndingBlank after each fence to lineEnding in each child flow's events before subtokenize, and moves container exit events so trailing blank lines and lazy lines attach as they did; a lazyContentEnd construct registered under the null code ends a block on a line that does not reach it, as the old sub-document did.
The 32 bound counts only directive containers open around the line, recorded by continuations; a start only reads the record, so micromark's effects.check cannot fool it.
The renderer now writes a leading rule as *** before a top-level typed block, since a --- there would read back as an unclosed front-matter opener that turns the typed block into text.
nesting_test.go's 100-block 'callouts' row became 'callouts inside quotes' (68/69 quotes around 32 callouts), since 100 nested callouts now hit the 32 bound first.
deviations: Base e2e negative control: the first input fails by Playwright's 30 s test timeout, not the 15 s expect timeout the plan predicted (the parse holds the main thread longer than the test).

Residual reading difference found by fuzzing old vs new (2 of 120,000 random documents): a footnote definition inside a ::: block now also defines its footnote for a call earlier in the text; recorded in the CHANGELOG. No committed fixture or differential corpus document carries it.
The default-mode refusal of a bounded opener checks paragraph lines, like the existing rule: a bounded opener that becomes a setext heading is not refused in the browser (Go refuses that write).
